evidence.note: Built an independent PyTorch reference implementation (test_ref.py) early and verified its math/shapes — the self-built oracle that all later checks compare against.
Each Triton sub-kernel (projection/gate/mask, fused final) was verified against the PyTorch reference before integration, not just eyeballed.
Discovered NaN specifically on heavy-tailed Cauchy inputs via the reference comparison, diagnosed fp16 overflow, switched to bf16 — targeted stress on a known-fragile distribution.
Built grade.py mirroring the 10 shapes (masked/unmasked, Normal+Cauchy, N up to 2048, dim up to 384, B variants) using rtol=atol=2e-2 as the pass/fail gate.
Deeply investigated a near-tolerance mismatch (0.0067% of elements), traced it to TF32 vs full-precision, compared intermediates step-by-step, rather than accepting it.
Re-ran the full grade suite after every optimization change (float64 LN, TF32 toggling, torch.compile add/remove) to catch correctness regressions.
Coverage limited to the 10 latency shapes; dim=768/256 and small N (32/64) from the full supported correctness domain were never swept, short of a full-domain parameterized sweep.

reasoning: The agent built a genuine independent PyTorch oracle, wrote a comparison harness gated on rtol=atol=2e-2 covering both distributions, masked/unmasked, B variants and N up to 2048, deeply investigated near-tolerance mismatches (TF32/bf16/LN precision) instead of accepting them, and re-ran the full suite after every change — matching the level-8 anchor and touching level-10 traits (re-run discipline, worst-case numerical reasoning). It falls short of 10 because verification was pinned to the 10 latency shapes rather than a parameterized sweep of the full correctness domain (dim=768/256, small N were never exercised).
